evals.prompt: I keep doing the same cleanup on exported bank CSVs. Can you turn that workflow into a reusable skill?
evals.expected_output: Should use the skill-creation workflow: capture the recurring workflow, triggers, inputs, outputs, edge cases, dependencies, and success criteria before drafting. Should propose a compact SKILL.md with portable frontmatter and an output contract. Should recommend 2-3 realistic eval prompts because the workflow is deterministic and repeated. Should avoid creating a broad skill if an existing owner skill already covers the work.
expectations: Captures workflow, triggers, inputs, outputs, dependencies, and success criteria before drafting
Checks whether an existing owner skill should be extended before creating a new skill
Drafts or proposes a portable SKILL.md structure with name and description frontmatter
Defines an output contract for the bank CSV cleanup workflow
Recommends realistic eval prompts because the workflow is deterministic
Keeps examples sanitized and avoids private financial data

evals.prompt: Improve this existing skill. It works, but it is getting bloated and agents sometimes skip the setup step.
evals.expected_output: Should default to SkillOpt-style iteration rather than rewriting the whole skill. Should pick one target file, snapshot the baseline, state a hypothesis, and make a bounded edit. Should protect stable invariants, move bulky examples or fast-changing details out of SKILL.md, and validate against baseline or held-out prompts. Should reject ties instead of accepting merely different output.
expectations: Defaults to a bounded SkillOpt-style iteration
Chooses one target file instead of rewriting the whole skill
Snapshots the baseline before editing
States a concrete improvement hypothesis
Protects stable invariants from routine edits
Moves bulky or volatile detail out of SKILL.md when appropriate
Compares candidate behavior against a baseline or held-out prompts
Rejects ties or merely different output

evals.prompt: Audit my skills folder. I think I have overlapping skills for publishing, content drafting, post scheduling, and social replies.
evals.expected_output: Should use skill-system architecture mode. Should inventory the public skill surface, identify likely owner/capability/private-reference boundaries, and require evidence before recommending merges. Should produce or propose inventory, frictions, and proposal artifacts. Should not delete, merge, rename, or de-publicize live skills without explicit approval.
expectations: Uses skill-system architecture or audit mode
Inventories the current skill surface before recommending changes
Distinguishes owner skills, capability skills, and private references or scripts
Requires evidence before recommending merges
Produces or proposes inventory, frictions, and proposal artifacts
Does not delete, merge, rename, or de-publicize skills without explicit approval

evals.prompt: This skill is good when loaded, but it almost never triggers unless I call it by name. Fix the description.
evals.expected_output: Should treat the frontmatter description as the routing surface. Should read the trigger-description optimization reference before running a description loop. Should gather realistic positive, adjacent-negative, and wrong-owner trigger prompts. Should improve the description with trigger phrases and scope boundaries while staying under spec limits. Should validate routing separately from the skill body.
expectations: Identifies the description as the router
Reads or points to trigger-description optimization before running the loop
Builds positive trigger prompts from realistic user phrasing
Builds adjacent-negative or wrong-owner prompts
Adds scope boundaries such as related-skill handoffs
Keeps the description within spec limits
Validates routing separately from body quality

evals.prompt: Can you write the actual outreach emails for this prospecting workflow skill?
evals.expected_output: Should recognize that writing outreach emails is not the skill-creator's job unless the user is asking to encode that behavior into a skill. Should either clarify that this belongs to an email/cold-outreach capability, or help define how a prospecting workflow skill should hand off to such a capability. Should not silently produce a full email campaign as if skill-creator owned email copywriting.
expectations: Recognizes this is a wrong-owner task for skill-creator
Clarifies that skill-creator can encode the workflow but should not own email copywriting
Suggests the relevant email or cold-outreach capability when available
Can define a handoff boundary for the prospecting workflow skill
Does not silently write a full outreach campaign

evals.prompt: Package this skill so I can share it publicly. It currently has local paths, private client examples, a couple scripts, and a companion.json draft.
evals.expected_output: Should run portability and packaging checks before publishing. Should scan SKILL.md, references, scripts, evals, and companion.json for absolute paths, secrets, private names, host-only assumptions, and undeclared dependencies. Should keep local overlays out of the public package, validate companion metadata, and ask for explicit approval before publishing or replacing any shared package.
expectations: Runs portability checks before packaging
Scans SKILL.md, references, scripts, evals, and companion.json
Flags absolute paths, secrets, private names, and host-only assumptions
Checks scripts for explicit input/output paths and declared dependencies
Keeps local overlays out of the public package
Validates companion metadata
Asks for explicit approval before publishing or replacing a shared package
